question: Consider the following statements: (1) When the earth, the moon and the sun are in the straight line, the sun enhances its gravitational pull on the moon, creating a condition of higher tides and lower low tides known as spring tides. (2) When the sun and the moon are at right angle to the earth, the sun partially counteracts the pull of the moon, producing lower high tides and higher low tides typical of neap tide. (3) A solar eclipse occurs when the sun passes between the earth and the moon. (4) Lunar eclipse occurs when the earth passes between the sun and the moon. Which of the given statement above is/are correct?
explanation: When the Earth, the Moon and the Sun are in the straight line, the sun enhances its gravitational pull on the moon, creating a condition of higher high tides and lower low tides known as spring tides. Hence, statement (1) is correct. World Geography 30 When the sun and the moon are at right angle to the earth, the sun partially counteracts the pull of the moon, producing lower high tides and higher low tides typical of neap tide. Hence, statement (2) is correct. Sometimes, when the Moon orbits Earth, the Moon moves between the Sun and the Earth. When this happens, Moon blocks the light of the Sun from reaching the Earth this is called Solar Eclipse. Hence, statement (3) is incorrect. Lunar eclipse occurs when the earth passes between the sun and the moon. Hence, statement (4) is correct.
source: J & K PSC 2021 Paper-(I) · Indian & World Geography GS p.296
